=== CONSULTING BRIEF (every field below is mandatory grounding for the prototype) ===
Thesis: An Azure OpenAI script that reads a student's Common App and admissions essay to populate their baseline CLR profile before Day One.
Description (what gets built):
The biggest hurdle to CLR adoption is the 'cold start' problem—students arrive with blank profiles and are asked to fill them out. This tool bypasses that entirely. It securely processes the unstructured data submitted during the admissions process (resumes, essays, Common App activities). It maps high school achievements to the CLR taxonomy. When first-year undergraduate students log in for the first time, their profile is already 40% complete. They simply review and approve. It turns a chore into a moment of delight and institutional recognition.
Why it matters for first-year undergraduate students:
First-year undergraduate students arrive with valuable prior experience that the university immediately loses track of. By capturing this data instantly, first-year undergraduate students feel seen and valued, and their first advisor meeting can focus on strategy rather than data gathering.
How it supports first-year undergraduate students outcomes over first 18-24 months:
Solving the cold-start problem in the first 18-24 months ensures high adoption of the CLR. A highly adopted CLR leads directly to better matching, better advising, and ultimately higher placement rates in year three.
Comprehensive Learner Record (CLR) dependency / independence rationale:
This is a pure CLR enablement play. It requires the CLR infrastructure to exist so there is a destination for the extracted admissions data. Without the CLR, the data has nowhere to go.
Execution within Northeastern University's existing stack (named systems, connectors, AI layer location):
Runs as a secure batch process in Azure OpenAI, moving data from the Slate admissions CRM into the Salesforce/Snowflake CLR backend.
Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, SharePoint, Power Automate, Power BI, Azure OpenAI fit (named tools that reduce cost/burden):
Leverages Azure OpenAI for the extraction, keeping all PII and FERPA-protected data strictly within the university's managed tenant.
Key stakeholders:
  1. Liz Zulick — Champions the solution to drive CLR adoption.
  2. Jen — Manages the data pipeline from Slate to Snowflake.
  3. Admissions Office — Approves the use of admissions data for student success purposes.
Implementation steps (the prototype should visibly demonstrate at least one of these in action):
  Step 1: Secure data sharing agreement with Admissions (owner: Liz Zulick, effort: 4 weeks)
  Step 2: Build Azure OpenAI extraction pipeline for Common App PDFs (owner: NXT Humans, effort: 4 weeks, deps: Data access)
  Step 3: Map extracted high school activities to CLR taxonomy (owner: Liz Zulick, effort: 2 weeks, deps: Extraction pipeline)
  Step 4: Design the 'Review & Approve' onboarding screen in SharePoint (owner: Jen, effort: 2 weeks, deps: Taxonomy mapping)
Risks & mitigations (surface relevant risks as in-product safeguards or copy):
  1. [HIGH] Admissions data is legally siloed → Require students to click an opt-in consent box during enrollment deposit to allow data transfer.
  2. [MEDIUM] High school skills don't map cleanly to employer skills → Create a specific 'Pre-College' tier in the CLR taxonomy.
  3. [LOW] Hallucinations in extraction → Student must manually approve the imported items.
Guardrail fit (why this passes the Liz Zulick & Jen & Chris meeting filter — preserve this rationale visually in the prototype):
Directly solves Ben's 'manual data entry' non-starter. Aligns with Liz's vision for an 'anti-melt tool' that engages the student before they even arrive.
Expected impact metrics (surface as live KPI badges where appropriate):
Achieve an 85% completion rate for baseline CLR profiles on Day One of the fall semester.

The "aha" interaction (the single moment the user feels the product working): The portal welcomes them and shows their CLR profile already populated with 'Debate Team Captain' and 'Python Certification' extracted from their admissions file.

Existing stack to reuse: Slate (Admissions CRM), Azure OpenAI, Salesforce, Snowflake

=== GROUNDING THEMES (cited by this concept) ===
  1. AI-Driven First-Year Readiness Interventions
    Thesis: Students are arriving at the university increasingly unprepared for the rigorous co-op search process, lacking foundational resume and interview skills. To combat this, institutions are deploying AI-enabled readiness roadmaps that ingest admissions data to baseline skills before formal human advising begins. This early intervention shifts the burden of basic career reflection away from 1:1 advisor meetings.

  2. Stealth Implementation of Comprehensive Learner Record
    Thesis: Past failures with large-scale platforms, specifically the Student Assessed Integrated Learning (SAIL) initiative, have created institutional resistance to comprehensive system pitches. Leadership advises that new AI and CLR initiatives must be framed as bite-sized, tactical interventions. By embedding data collection quietly within high-utility first-year readiness tools, the university can build comprehensive learner profiles without triggering executive scrutiny.

  3. System Fragmentation and Shadow IT Workarounds
    Thesis: The student digital ecosystem is highly fragmented, requiring users to navigate up to 20 disconnected systems from initial search through matriculation. This lack of a unified platform forces students to engineer their own shadow IT workarounds, such as personal spreadsheets, to track co-op applications. Consequently, the university loses critical data visibility into the co-op pipeline.

=== RESEARCH GOAL (the engagement question this prototype helps answer) ===
Identify a comprehensive new strategy for co-op based on the current statement of work for NU, prior projects with NU, and fresh industry analysis of experiential learning and co-op engagement tactics to improve learner's chances of gaining meaningful experiential learning opportunities from pre-enrollment to graduate school
=== BUILD INSTRUCTIONS ===
Think ultra hard about the persona's actual pain points above. Build a multi-screen experience that:
  1. Opens in a state reflecting the persona's actual emotional/situational reality (not a generic "welcome"). Reference their context from the FULL PERSONA PROFILE.
  2. Demonstrates the implementation steps from the BRIEF as live, working interactions — at least 1-2 of those steps should be a screen the user navigates to and an AI flow they fire.
  3. Uses verbatim quotes from the THEMES / verbatim_quote_evidence block as in-product evidence/testimonials — NEVER lorem ipsum.
  4. References the persona by their real name throughout. Names from the uploads should appear in seed data (real co-op partners, real programs).
  5. Demonstrates the "aha" interaction explicitly as one screen-or-state with the AI call wired LIVE to /api/ai/gemini-compat (or /api/ai/anthropic, /api/wiki/fetch-articles depending on capability).
  6. Surfaces the expected_impact metrics as visible KPI badges where natural.
  7. Honors every guardrail in guardrail_fit — visibly. If "no new platform" is in the guardrails, the prototype's chrome should communicate "this lives inside [existing system]" (e.g., a Copilot Studio badge in the header).

brief.frame_rationale: By shifting the interaction to a celebratory, stealth 'anti-melt' welcome moment in the Admitted Student SharePoint rather than a formal 'profile setup' chore, we honor the 'zero manual entry' constraint and Liz's vision of an early-access anti-melt tool.
brief.one_line_thesis: An Azure OpenAI pipeline that securely translates admissions essays into a 40%-complete Comprehensive Learner Record before Day One.

primary_persona.name: Maya
primary_persona.context: Incoming first-year undergraduate student who has high-school leadership experience (Debate Team Captain, Python Certification) but hasn't entered it into any university system. She is navigating up to 20 disconnected systems from initial search through matriculation.
primary_persona.emotional_state: Excited but overwhelmed by the fragmented onboarding process; dreads filling out another 20-page university form and wants to feel seen by the institution.

secondary_actors.involvement: Champions the solution to drive CLR adoption and monitors the '85% completion rate' KPI dashboard.
Manages the secure data pipeline from Slate to Snowflake, ensuring it stays within the Microsoft ecosystem.

brief.demonstrated_moment: August pre-arrival: Maya logs into the existing Northeastern Admitted Student SharePoint portal to check her orientation schedule and is greeted by a personalized, AI-generated welcome that has already drafted her CLR.
jobs_to_be_done: Bypass the 'cold start' problem by automatically extracting skills from my Common App so I don't have to manually enter them.
Review and approve my pre-populated university profile in a low-friction, zero-shame environment.
Feel recognized by the university for my prior achievements before I even step on campus, validating my choice to enroll.
success_criteria: The user, who lives the 'System Fragmentation' reality, feels immediate relief that they don't have to re-enter their high school resume.
Feels differentiated from generic SaaS by embedding the data collection quietly within a high-utility, celebratory welcome screen (Stealth Implementation).
Achieves the Liz Zulick guardrail: Zero manual data entry, no scoring/shaming, and operates entirely within the Microsoft/SharePoint ecosystem.
Visibly demonstrates the 'anti-melt' value by engaging the student with their own success narrative before Day One.

ai_inference_points.trigger: Simulated background batch process upon Maya's first login to the SharePoint portal.
ai_inference_points.input: Maya's unstructured Common App PDF (Essay about Debate Team, Activity List including Python Certification).
ai_inference_points.output_shape: JSON array of mapped CLR taxonomy skills (e.g., 'Public Speaking', 'Python') and a personalized welcome message celebrating these specific traits.
ai_inference_points.value_unlocked: Eliminates the cold-start problem and makes the student feel deeply understood without any manual data entry.

ai_inference_points.trigger: Maya clicks 'I did something else this summer' to add a recent experience not on her Common App.
ai_inference_points.input: Natural language input: 'I worked as a camp counselor in July'.
ai_inference_points.output_shape: Structured extraction mapping 'camp counselor' to CLR skills like 'Leadership' and 'Conflict Resolution', instantly added to the approval queue.
ai_inference_points.value_unlocked: Maintains the zero-manual-data-entry rule even for net-new information, keeping the interaction conversational and frictionless.

hard_constraints.accessibility: WCAG AA minimum, clear opt-in consent checkbox for FERPA compliance regarding admissions data transfer.
other: No brand-new standalone platform (must look like a SharePoint web part / Microsoft 365 Copilot surface).
No manual data entry for students (form fields are forbidden; use one-click approvals).
No scoring or shaming students (no red indicators for missing data).
Must include the verbatim quote in the UI or advisor view: 'It is an anti-melt tool. Maybe you could access it somewhere before you start.' — Liz

open_questions: How exactly does the 'Pre-College' tier in the CLR taxonomy map to employer-facing skills later in year 3?
What is the exact FERPA consent language required during the enrollment deposit phase to legally un-silo the Slate admissions data?
How do we handle hallucinations if the AI extracts a skill the student didn't actually claim in their essay?

behavior_per_state.default: Subtle gray outline, white background, dark text. Looks like a suggestion.
behavior_per_state.hover: Outline turns NU Red, cursor changes to pointer, slight upward translation (y: -2px).
behavior_per_state.active: Scale down to 0.95, background fills with light gray.
behavior_per_state.success: Background fills with NU Red, text turns white, a small checkmark icon animates in from the left.

behavior_per_state.default: Standard text input field with a muted send icon.
behavior_per_state.active: Border glows with SharePoint Blue focus ring.
behavior_per_state.loading: Input disables, send icon replaces with a spinning loader, shimmering 'Extracting skills...' placeholder text.
behavior_per_state.success: Input clears, collapses slightly, and a success toast appears above it.
behavior_per_state.empty: Send button disabled until text is entered.
behavior_per_state.error: Border turns red, helper text says 'We couldn't process that. Try again?'

motion_contract.encodes: System is working in the background (shimmering gradient from light gray to white) without blocking the user from viewing their orientation schedule.
Celebration and personalization. The text fades in line-by-line, making it feel like a bespoke message being delivered rather than a static database pull.
State change from 'suggested' to 'owned'. Upon clicking approve, the chips physically slide down into the 'Pre-College CLR' container.
Progressive disclosure. The panel expands smoothly from the bottom of the web part only when the user explicitly asks to add more, keeping the initial view uncluttered.
Context switch. The font weight and styling shift from student-facing (friendly, rounded) to advisor-facing (dense, analytical, bold metrics).

critique.summary: The prototype successfully implements the core anti-melt CLR extraction flow, including both the Common App and Summer Chat AI integrations. However, it introduces several rogue hex colors not defined in the design system and fails to implement the exact micro-interaction spec for the approved SkillChip state.

issues.description: The code introduces multiple rogue colors not present in the Design System (e.g., #F0F0F0, #737373, #FBE7EA, #E6F3EB, #333, #0056b3). All colors must map strictly to the provided color_system tokens.
issues.code_location: injectStyles() and inline styles throughout the components
issues.fix: Replace all rogue hex codes with valid CSS variables derived from the Design System (e.g., use var(--nu-surface) instead of #F0F0F0, var(--nu-text-secondary) instead of #737373, var(--nu-cream) instead of #FBE7EA).

issues.description: The SkillChip success state does not match the micro-interaction spec. The spec requires the background to fill with NU Red and text to turn white, with a checkmark animating in from the left. The code uses a rogue light green background with green text.
issues.fix: Update the SkillChip success state to use var(--nu-red) for the background, var(--nu-bg) for the text, and position the checkmark icon to the left of the label.

issues.description: The AI fetch calls use the endpoint '/api/ai/gemini-compat' instead of the specified '/api/ai/openai'.
